Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 101, verses 1–11:

It is Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

{1–3} {Al-Qari'ah} (The Striking Calamity): one of the names of the Day of Resurrection. It is so called because it strikes people and disturbs them with its terrors. For this reason its matter is magnified and emphasized in His saying: {The Striking Calamity. What is the Striking Calamity? And what will make you know what the Striking Calamity is?}

{4} {The Day when mankind will be like scattered moths}: because of the intensity of fear and terror; that is, like scattered locusts, some of which surge over others. Al-farash (moths) are creatures that swarm over one another at night, not knowing where to head; when a fire is kindled for them, they rush into it because of the weakness of their perception. Such is the state of people, who possess intellects.

{5} As for the mountains, the solid and hard, they will be {like wool carded}; that is, like carded wool that has become so weak that the slightest wind carries it away. Allah the Exalted said: {And you see the mountains, thinking them solid, while they pass away as the passing of clouds}. Then after that they will become {scattered dust}, vanishing so that nothing of them remains to be seen. Then the scales will be set up, and people will be divided into two groups: the happy and the wretched.

{6–7} {As for him whose scales are heavy}; that is, whose good deeds outweigh his bad deeds, {he will be in a pleasing life}: in the Gardens of Bliss.

{8–11} {And as for him whose scales are light}: meaning he has no good deeds to counterbalance his bad deeds, {his mother is the Abyss}; that is, his refuge and dwelling is the Fire, which is among its names al-Hawiyah (the Abyss). It will be for him like a constant mother, as Allah the Exalted said: {Indeed, its punishment is ever adhering}. It has also been said that the meaning of this is: his mother of the brain is an abyss in the Fire; that is, he will be thrown into the Fire headfirst. {And what will make you know what it is?} This is a magnification of its matter. Then He explained it by His saying: {A fierce Fire}; that is, extremely hot, its heat having exceeded the heat of the fire of this world by seventy times. We seek refuge with Allah from it.
